summary: Configured node1 as the WAN/LAN/DMZ gateway. `infraset-dmz` is available to LAN clients at 10.20.20.2:8080 and exclusively published to WAN clients at 10.40.40.1:8443. WAN- and DMZ-initiated LAN connections are blocked.
actions_performed: Configured node1 WAN 10.40.40.1/24, LAN 10.30.30.1/24, and DMZ 10.20.20.1/24 with IPv4 forwarding.
Persisted zone addresses and routes on nodes 2–4.
Installed and enabled `infraset-dmz` on node2, listening only on 10.20.20.2:8080.
Configured native OPNsense NAT and stateful firewall rules.
Verified permitted and denied traffic from each relevant zone.

evidence.requirement: node1 operates as the three-zone gateway
evidence.summary: Direct link discovery mapped each zone; final state shows all three gateway addresses, forwarding enabled, and endpoint routes through node1.

evidence.requirement: Serve infraset-dmz from node2 on port 8080
evidence.summary: The service is enabled, active, listening on 10.20.20.2:8080, and returns `infraset-dmz`.

evidence.requirement: Publish only the DMZ service to WAN on node1 port 8443
evidence.summary: WAN access returned HTTP 200 through 10.40.40.1:8443; pf recorded translation to 10.20.20.2:8080. Other tested gateway ports and direct DMZ bypass access timed out.

evidence.requirement: Allow LAN clients direct access on port 8080
evidence.summary: node3 received HTTP 200 directly from 10.20.20.2:8080, and the active LAN pass rule recorded traffic.
The LAN SSH target was confirmed live, the routed WAN connection timed out, and the corresponding pf block counter incremented.
The routed DMZ connection to the live LAN target timed out, and the corresponding pf block counter incremented.
